question: If all of a borrower's federal student loans were disbursed on or after July 1, 2026, which income-driven repayment plan is the only one available to them?
answer:
If all of your loans were disbursed on or after July 1, 2026, the only income-driven repayment plan available is the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP) [7]. RAP is open to Direct Loans disbursed at any time [1]. The Tiered Standard Plan is also available to these borrowers, but it is a fixed-payment plan rather than an income-driven one [1][4].

Parent PLUS loans are an exception. They can be repaid only under the Tiered Standard Plan [4]. A separate source says new parent PLUS loans made after July 1, 2026 are ineligible for income-driven repayment [6].

studyNotes.focus: The question asks which single income-driven repayment plan is the only IDR option for a borrower whose federal loans were all first disbursed on or after July 1, 2026.

keyPoints.text: If all of a borrower's loans were disbursed on or after July 1, 2026, the only IDR plan available is the Repayment Assistance Plan (RAP).
RAP applies to Direct Loans disbursed at any time, while IBR, ICR, and PAYE apply only to loans disbursed before July 1, 2026.
Borrowers with any loan disbursed on or after July 1, 2026 must repay all eligible Direct Loans under RAP or the Tiered Standard Plan.
The Tiered Standard Plan is a fixed-payment option, not an income-driven plan, so it does not answer the IDR question.
